name: Postgres 18 + pgvector Vector Database
description: Drop-in Postgres with pgvector, pooling and backups for RAG and embeddings.

Postgres.startCommand: /usr/bin/tini -g -- /bin/bash -c 'set -e; D="${PGDATA%/}"; F="$D/pgvector-tuning.conf"; C="$D/postgresql.conf"; I=/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d; X=/tmp/pgvector-tuning.conf; echo "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;" > $I/zz-pgvector-extensions.sql; k() { v=$1; if [ $v -lt $2 ]; then v=$2; fi; if [ $v -gt $3 ]; then v=$3; fi; echo $v; }; n() { case "$1" in ""|*[!0-9]*) echo $2 ;; *) echo $1 ;; esac; }; w() { echo "$1 = $2" >> $X; }; if [ "${PGVECTOR_TUNING:-auto}" = off ]; then rm -f $F $I/zz-pgvector-conf.sh; echo "pgvector-tune: PGVECTOR_TUNING=off, Postgres defaults apply"; else H=$(( $(n "$(grep -m 1 MemTotal /proc/meminfo | tr -s " " | cut -d " " -f 2)" 1048576) / 1024 )); M=$(( $(n "$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max 2>/dev/null)" $((H * 1048576))) / 1048576 )); if [ $M -gt $H ]; then M=$H; fi; B=$(k $(n "$PG_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB" $(k $M 256 8192)) 256 4194304); N=$(nproc); read -r Q P 2>/dev/null < /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max || Q=max; case "$Q" in ""|*[!0-9]*) ;; *) N=$(k $(( (Q + P - 1) / P )) 1 $N) ;; esac; N=$(k $(n "$PG_CPU_LIMIT" $(k $N 1 8)) 1 256); S=$(( $(n "$(df -Pk /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | tr -s " " | cut -d " " -f 2)" 65536) / 1024 )); SB=$(k $((B / 4)) 128 1048576); MW=$(k $((B / 4)) 64 2048); PM=$(k $((N - 1)) 0 4); PW=$(k $N 2 256); PG=$(k $((N / 2)) 0 2); FIT=$((S * 3 / 4)); if [ $FIT -lt 128 ]; then PM=0; fi; if [ $PM -gt 0 ]; then MW=$(k $MW 64 $FIT); fi; if [ $S -lt 256 ]; then PG=0; fi; echo "# pgvector template: rewritten at every boot from budget ${B}MB (container ${M}MB), ${N} cpus, /dev/shm ${S}MB; ALTER SYSTEM overrides it" > $X; w shared_buffers ${SB}MB; w effective_cache_size $((B * 3 / 4))MB; w maintenance_work_mem ${MW}MB; w autovacuum_work_mem $(k $((B / 16)) 64 $MW)MB; w work_mem $(k $((B / 512)) 4 64)MB; w max_worker_processes $(k $((PW + 4)) 8 512); w max_parallel_workers $PW; w max_parallel_workers_per_gather $PG; w max_parallel_maintenance_workers $PM; w random_page_cost 1.1; w effective_io_concurrency 200; w track_io_timing on; chmod 644 $X; if [ -f $D/PG_VERSION ] && [ -f $C ]; then install -o postgres -g postgres -m 600 $X $F; grep -qsF "include_if_exists = pgvector-tuning.conf" $C || echo "include_if_exists = pgvector-tuning.conf" >> $C; sync $F $C 2>/dev/null || true; else echo "cp $X $F && chmod 600 $F && { grep -qsF pgvector-tuning.conf $C || echo include_if_exists = pgvector-tuning.conf >> $C; }" > $I/zz-pgvector-conf.sh; fi; echo "pgvector-tune: $(paste -sd " " $X)"; fi; exec /usr/local/bin/wrapper.sh "$@"' pgvector-start postgres -p 5432 -c listen_addresses=*

PGDATA.description: Data directory inside the volume (Railway base layout; the image refuses to start with anything outside /var/lib/postgresql/data).

PGHOST.description: Private hostname of this database (postgres.railway.internal). Used by the Data panel and by the services that reference it.

PGPORT.description: Postgres port (the image always listens on 5432).

PGUSER.description: User for the Data panel and libpq clients.

PGPASSWORD.description: Password for the Data panel and libpq clients.

PGDATABASE.description: Default database for the Data panel and libpq clients.

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.description: Superuser password, generated at deploy (letters only, so it is URL-safe). Changing it later needs ALTER USER as well.

POSTGRES_DB.description: Database created on first boot; the vector and pg_stat_statements extensions are created in it.

DATABASE_URL.description: Direct connection over the private network. Use it for migrations, index builds and session features (LISTEN/NOTIFY, advisory locks, SET).

DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL.description: Connection from outside Railway through the TCP proxy (egress is billed). Add sslmode=require for psql/libpq; the certificate is self-signed.

DATABASE_POOL_URL.description: Pooled connection through PgBouncer (transaction mode, private network only). Use it for application queries.

SSL_CERT_DAYS.description: Validity of the self-signed TLS certificate; it is renewed on a redeploy within 30 days of expiry.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Time Postgres gets to shut down cleanly on redeploy.

RAILWAY_SHM_SIZE_BYTES.description: Size of /dev/shm (1 GiB; Railway default 64 MB). Parallel HNSW builds keep the graph in shared memory; only memory in use is billed.

PGVECTOR_TUNING.description: auto = size memory and parallelism from the container limits at every boot (pgvector-tuning.conf); off = Postgres and Railway defaults.

PG_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB.description: RAM the tuning plans for. auto = the container limit capped at 8192 MB; set a number (e.g. 16384) after raising the service's memory.

PG_CPU_LIMIT.description: CPUs the tuning plans for (parallel workers). auto = the container CPU quota capped at 8; set a number to override.

DB_HOST.description: Postgres private hostname that PgBouncer forwards to.

DB_USER.description: Postgres superuser; written to PgBouncer's userlist and used as auth_user, so other roles can log in through the pool too.

DB_PASSWORD.description: Password of that user (kept in sync by reference).

AUTH_TYPE.description: Client authentication; matches Postgres' SCRAM password encryption.

LISTEN_ADDR.description: Listen on all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (Railway's private network can be IPv6-only).

LISTEN_PORT.description: PgBouncer port on the private network.

POOL_MODE.description: transaction = a server connection per transaction (best multiplexing). Use session for apps that need session state.

DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE.description: Server connections per database/user pair; keep the total under Postgres max_connections (500 on Railway's image).

MAX_PREPARED_STATEMENTS.description: Protocol-level prepared statements tracked per connection, so drivers that prepare statements work in transaction mode. 0 disables.

ADMIN_USERS.description: Users allowed to run SHOW POOLS / SHOW STATS on the pgbouncer admin database.

DATABASE_POOL_URL.description: Pooled connection string for your apps (also exposed on the Postgres service). No TLS: it stays on the private network.

PGUSER.description: Superuser, needed to dump roles and every database.

PGDATABASE.description: Database used to list the others.

PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds before a connection attempt gives up (the job retries while Postgres starts).

PGAPPNAME.description: application_name shown in pg_stat_activity while a backup runs.

BACKUP_S3_BUCKET.description: Railway Bucket that stores the backups.

BACKUP_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE.description: Keep false: Railway Buckets use virtual-hosted-style URLs. true only for buckets whose Credentials tab says path-style.

BACKUP_PREFIX.description: Folder in the bucket; each run writes {prefix}/{UTC timestamp}/.

BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS.description: Delete complete runs older than this many days.

BACKUP_KEEP_MIN.description: Always keep at least this many complete runs, whatever their age.

BACKUP_COMPRESSION.description: pg_dump --compress value for the custom-format dumps (zstd:3, gzip:6, lz4, none).

BACKUP_DATABASES.description: Databases to dump, comma-separated. Empty = every database that accepts connections.

BACKUP_WAIT_SECONDS.description: How long a run waits for Postgres to accept connections before failing.
